A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a method for structure-from-motion and symmetry detection for urban facade reconstruction, and we also demonstrate that such a method can lead to new image editing operations.

we present a framework that enables a range of image editing operations on urban facades that maintain consistency across images, and that we show the robustness of our method on a range of examples containing repetitions and nondistictive features.

The main takeaway from our work is that
symmetry information is crucial for robustly handling repeated structures in unordered sets of images, and that the geometry of the scene is important for the symmetry detection process.
the problem of symmetry detection in unordered images is not a post-processing step, but a core part of the 3D reconstruction process.
symmetry detection and structure-from-motion can be coupled together to produce more accurate 3D reconstructions.
